significance: Richard de Ledrede, Bishop of Ossory, brought composite witchcraft charges against Alice Kyteler and twelve associates — the earliest substantially documented composite witchcraft prosecution in the British Isles and one of the earliest in Europe, predating the Alpine trials by a century.
source_method: Chronicle of the proceedings against Dame Alice Kyteler (attributed to contemporaries, ed. Thomas Wright, 1843); analyzed in Hutton, The Witch (2017); Ankarloo and Clark Vol. 3 (2002)
